Indicator 4a1 measures the proportion of patients with atrial fibrillation and an indication for anticoagulation treatment who receive the treatment one year after their index date. The national standard for this indicator is set at ≥ 90%.

In the 2022/23 reporting period, the national average for [[danmark|Danmark]] was 89.1%, meaning the country as a whole missed the target [^src1]. Among the five administrative regions, only [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] met the standard with a score of 92.1% [^src1]. The remaining regions fell short: [[region-midtjylland|Region Midtjylland]] (89.2%), [[region-hovedstaden|Region Hovedstaden]] (88.8%), [[region-sjaelland|Region Sjælland]] (88.7%), and [[region-syddanmark|Region Syddanmark]] (88.2%) [^src1].

Performance at the health cluster level revealed significant outliers. The highest-performing cluster was [[klynge-vest|Klynge VEST]] at 94.7%, followed by [[klynge-syd|Klynge SYD]] (92.7%) and Klynge MIDT (92.3%) [^src1]. Other clusters successfully meeting the ≥ 90% threshold included [[sundhedsklynge-bornholm|Sundhedsklynge Bornholm]] (91.8%), [[horsensklyngen|Horsensklyngen]] (91.3%), [[randersklyngen|Randersklyngen]] (91.2%), [[klynge-nord|Klynge NORD]] (90.8%), [[sundhedsklynge-lillebaelt|Sundhedsklynge Lillebælt]] (90.4%), and [[sundhedsklyngen-suh|Sundhedsklyngen SUH]] (90.3%) [^src1]. 

Conversely, the lowest-performing clusters were [[sundhedsklyngen-nykoebing-f|Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F]] at 85.1%, [[sundhedsklynge-soenderjylland|Sundhedsklynge Sønderjylland]] at 87.2%, and both [[sundhedsklynge-fyn|Sundhedsklynge Fyn]] and [[goedstrupklyngen|Gødstrupklyngen]] at 87.4% [^src1]. 

While this single dated section does not support a multi-report trend analysis, the table's internal historical columns show notable shifts for specific clusters over the preceding years. For instance, [[klynge-vest|Klynge VEST]] improved from 90.6% in 2020/21 to 94.7% in 2022/23, whereas [[sundhedsklyngen-nykoebing-f|Sundhedsklyngen Nykøbing F]] experienced a sharp decline from 91.1% in 2021/22 to 85.1% in 2022/23 [^src1].
